artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Beatmaker" is a 2022 single by Matt Berry featuring UK soul singer Emma Noble, released on Acid Jazz Records. The track is a cover of the 1970 Swedish psych-funk song originally performed by Doris. Berry’s version reimagines the song with a vibrant blend of jazz and funk/soul, showcasing his knack for reviving vintage sounds with contemporary flair. The collaboration highlights Noble’s soulful vocals alongside Berry’s signature production style, resulting in a groove-driven, retro-inspired recording that fits seamlessly within Acid Jazz’s catalog.

While "Beatmaker" stands as a standalone single rather than a full album, it marks a notable moment in Matt Berry’s discography for its collaborative nature and stylistic departure from his more introspective, song-driven works like Phantom Birds or The Blue Elephant. The release was well-received by fans and critics for its energetic reinterpretation and authentic retro feel, further cementing Berry’s reputation as a versatile artist unafraid to explore diverse musical genres. Its inclusion in the soundtrack for the first episode of Toast of Tinseltown also brought the track wider exposure, reinforcing Berry’s dual presence in both music and television.
